title: C01-E007 - The Saint of the Open Hand

lines: The Saint of the Open Hand

cues.title: The Saint of the Open Hand
cues.subtitle: Campaign 1: The Lantern Road  -  Level 1  -  5 Emberfall 1047 AK
cues.text: Two days ago Lantern Thirty-Seven went dark outside the village of Brindle Cross. Brannoc the soldier, Ilsevel the archivist, Tamsin the card player and Oriel the priestess followed a goblin trail into Thornpike Woods, fought wolves and goblins, and found the lantern's core had been stolen by hand. They are coming home with three dead cores, and more questions than they left with.
Brindle Cross  -  Coming Home  -  Day
Brindle Cross, the afternoon of the fifth.
Four travellers come up the south road, filthy and tired, carrying something wrapped in a soldier's cloak.
Well? Is it lit?
cues.speaker: maddy_fenn

cues.text: No. But we know why it went out. Somebody took its core. By hand.
cues.speaker: ilsevel

cues.text: Brannoc opens the cloak. Three cloudy grey stones lie in it like eggs gone cold.
Three? We only lost the one! Whose are the other two? And who's paying for all this, the Eight?
cues.speaker: maddy_fenn

cues.text: The goblins, technically. They just don't know it yet.
cues.speaker: tamsin

cues.text: Father Tobin comes down from the shrine as fast as his cane allows, which is not very fast.
Oriel. Let me look at you. Are you hurt? Have you eaten? You haven't. I can tell by your ears.
cues.speaker: tobin_ashdown

cues.text: Father! I'm well. Better than well. These are my friends: Brannoc, Ilsevel, and Tam.
cues.speaker: oriel

cues.text: Brannoc. The silver in my alms box. I always wondered whose hand it came from.
cues.speaker: tobin_ashdown

cues.text: Supper at the shrine, all of you. There's soup. There's mostly soup.
cues.speaker: tobin_ashdown

cues.text: Supper's at my inn, Father, thank you. And the board is free, as I promised. Lantern lit or not.
cues.speaker: maddy_fenn

cues.text: Free! My favourite word, Mistress Fenn. You remembered.
cues.speaker: tamsin

cues.text: The Crooked Kettle (inside)  -  By the Hearth  -  Evening
That evening. The Crooked Kettle smells of mutton stew and woodsmoke, and Father Tobin has the best seat by the hearth.
Go on then, Father. Who was Saint Wenna? Sunshine says you tell it best.
cues.speaker: tamsin

cues.text: In the fourth year after the Kindling, every road in the world was dark. A woman named Wenna walked out of the last lit town.
cues.speaker: tobin_ashdown

cues.text: She carried a lantern in her open hand, and whoever she met on the road walked in its light.
cues.speaker: tobin_ashdown

cues.text: The fire pops. Even Maddy, behind the bar, stops wiping the same cup.
She never closed that hand. Not to fight, not to sleep. At the next town she lit a second lantern from the first, and walked on.
cues.speaker: tobin_ashdown

cues.text: 'The open hand holds more than the fist.' Forty years I've preached it. I still don't know if it's about lanterns or about people.
cues.speaker: tobin_ashdown

cues.text: The Order's own histories are rather more precise, Father. If I may.
cues.speaker: ilsevel

roll.purpose: c1: Recall what the Lamplighters' own histories say about Saint Wenna, the Order's founder, to set beside a village prie

cues.text: What comes back to Ilsevel is the first page of the Hall's primer, and not one word more.
'Saint Wenna founded the Order of Lamplighters in the fourth year After Kindling.' That is... the whole of the entry.
cues.speaker: ilsevel

cues.text: I like his better.
cues.speaker: tamsin

cues.text: So do I. I shall not be writing that down.
cues.speaker: ilsevel

cues.text: Oriel unwraps one of the dead cores and lays it in Father Tobin's hands.
Pray with me, Father? It should be warm. I want to know why it isn't.
cues.speaker: oriel

roll.purpose: c2: Hold a dead lantern-core and pray over it, trying to understand by faith why the flame will not come back to it.

cues.text: Oriel bows her head and reaches for the warmth she has felt since she was twelve. She feels nothing. Not the warmth. Not even the cold.
Nothing. It's as if it isn't there at all.
cues.speaker: oriel

cues.text: Then they'll sit on the altar, where the light is, until someone of the Order can see to them.
cues.speaker: tobin_ashdown

cues.text: I will write to Lamplighters' Hall tonight. Someone there can rekindle a core. In theory.
cues.speaker: ilsevel

cues.text: Father. Tell them my story. Please.
cues.speaker: oriel

cues.text: Your story. Very well. A frost night, in 1022. I was locking the shrine when I heard crying from Lantern No. 1.
cues.speaker: tobin_ashdown

cues.text: There you were at the foot of it, wrapped in a grey coat far too big for you, with a brass button at the collar.
cues.speaker: tobin_ashdown

cues.text: Oriel's fingers find the button on the cord at her neck. Tobin's eyes rest on it a moment too long, as they always do.
I named you Oriel. Golden. Because that lantern was the only light in the square, and you were in it.
cues.speaker: tobin_ashdown

cues.text: Good name.
cues.speaker: brannoc

cues.text: The Crooked Kettle (inside)  -  Forty-One  -  Evening
Mam! Father Tobin! Lantern Forty-One's gone dark! The carter saw it from the south road!
cues.speaker: wil_fenn

cues.text: Forty-One as well? And who's going to see to that one, the goblins?
cues.speaker: maddy_fenn

cues.text: And a rider came through at dusk, in Fort Harrow colours! He wouldn't stop. He left this for 'Bran Vow'.
cues.speaker: wil_fenn

cues.text: 'Bran Vow'? Big Man, is that you?
cues.speaker: tamsin

cues.text: Army name.
cues.speaker: brannoc

cues.text: Brannoc breaks the seal and reads, his lips moving slightly.
'Bran. Goblins seen near Wending Mill. Too many. I have no one to spare.'
cues.speaker: brannoc

cues.text: 'Look in on your way back. Bring help if you find any. Rook.'
cues.speaker: brannoc

cues.text: Wending Mill is on the road south. It is also, technically, where my inspection goes next.
cues.speaker: ilsevel

cues.text: Then we're the help.
cues.speaker: oriel

cues.text: Then go with my blessing. And come back, all of you. That part isn't in the scripture, but it should be.
cues.speaker: tobin_ashdown

cues.text: At dawn, then. Everyone sleeps. I'll take the...
cues.speaker: brannoc

cues.text: You'll sleep too, Brannoc.
cues.speaker: oriel

cues.text: ...Fine.
cues.speaker: brannoc

cues.text: Next time: Smoke on the road south. Wending Mill.
